tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

type.description: What kind of feedback this is.

title.description: Short, specific one-line summary of the issue.

details.description: Labeled bullets, in order: **What happened:** (observed vs. expected, exact error text if short); **What the user said:** (quoted, or "User didn't comment; observed by the model."); **Repro:** (minimal steps); **Evidence:** (request IDs, timestamps, paths, versions; omit if none); optionally a final **Cause:** only if verified in-session. One to three lines per bullet. No narrative paragraphs, no speculation, no secrets.

area.description: Optional short tag naming the part of Claude Code this is about (e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing"). Leave blank if unclear.

failure_mode.description: When the report is about MODEL BEHAVIOR (not a product bug), the closest failure mode, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value. Omit only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.

task_category.description: What kind of task the session was doing when the issue occurred, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: TaskStop
tools.description:
- Stops a running background task by its ID
- Takes a task_id parameter identifying the task to stop
- To stop an agent-team teammate, pass its agent ID or bare teammate name as task_id
- To stop a background agent spawned with a name, pass that name as task_id
- Returns a success or failure status
- Use this tool when you need to terminate a long-running task

task_id.description: The ID of the background task to stop. Agent-team teammates and named background agents are also accepted by agent ID or name.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: DeferredToolPlaceholder
tools.description: Reserved placeholder that keeps deferred tool loading active; never call this tool.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

- **Serving:** FastAPI serves it at `/`, and the same folder deploys as a static site. For a Vercel deploy, set the backend URL in `frontend/config.js` (`window.FINN_API_URL`). `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` doesn't apply, because there's no Next.js.
- **Tailwind notice:** the CDN build logs one "not for production" notice in the console. A production deploy would need compiled CSS, which needs Node.
- **Running now:** the backend is on `http://localhost:8000` (the app is at `/`). I restarted it once, to pick up the chat fallback change.

## Verified
I drove the app in headless Chrome at a 375px viewport and at desktop width. I used a temporary test page, now deleted.
- **Console and layout:** there were no console errors and no horizontal overflow at 375px.
- **Today:**
  - The alerts strip shows 7 alerts. The settings drawer works: demo thresholds raised it to 10, and "Reset defaults" returned it to 7.
  - Must Read shows 5 cards, Worth a Look shows 8, and All shows 100.
  - Results filings show a mini table with EBITDA margin, QoQ and YoY.
- **Research:**
  - Bajaj Finance loaded with the colour-coded Promised vs. Delivered card, six rows and four collapsible sections. Every item has citation badges.
  - An invalid ticker shows a clear "couldn't find it on Screener.in" message.
- **Chat:** the TCS catalysts and risks chip returned a cited answer with 10 citation pills, and clicking a pill opens the source excerpt.

## Not verified or not working
- **Chat "Compare…" chip:** the Bajaj ROA/ROE comparison failed, and the chat showed the error cleanly.
  - **Why:** Gemini was overloaded and returned 503/504 on the fallback model. The `gemini-3.5-flash` daily quota was also used up.
  - **What I changed:** comparison questions now fall back from `call_strong` to `call_cheap`, and the chat UI times out after 150 seconds. I couldn't re-test it end to end while Gemini was down. Please retry it later.
- **Browsers:** only Chrome was tested. I haven't tried Safari or a real phone.
- **Chat history:** it lives in page memory only, so it's lost on reload.
- **Filter limits:** the "All" and company filters show the top 100 filings by priority, from any date. Must Read and Worth a Look are limited to the last 7 days.

`DECISIONS.md` has a new entry, D30.

# FINN — AI investment assistant for Indian retail investors

FINN turns the daily flood of NSE/BSE corporate filings into a short, sourced digest, and lets you
ask questions that are answered only from company documents. It was built as a small working product
for the ENAM AI Engineer assessment, on free-tier infrastructure.

| Feature | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Push digest** | Classifies and scores every filing for an 18-company portfolio into *Must Read / Worth a Look / Routine*, with a one-line "why it matters". Results filings show extracted revenue / EBITDA / PBT / PAT with QoQ and YoY; management-change filings show who is joining or leaving, with a short background. |
| **Alerts** | Volume spikes, large price moves and material filings, with thresholds and watched categories the user can change live. |
| **Deep research** | For any NSE ticker: overview, financial health, growth catalysts and risks, built from the latest annual report and concall transcripts (via Screener.in), every bullet cited to a document and page. |
| **Promised vs. Delivered** | Finds specific, measurable commitments management made (annual report, older concalls) and checks them against later concalls and the latest quarterly results, with a status (*Beat / On Track / Delayed or Missed / Partially Disclosed*). |
| **Ask FINN** | Chat that retrieves from the stored documents, filings, results and prices and answers with inline citations such as `[Concall Q1 FY27, p. 22]`. |

The repository ships with a pre-populated database (`backend/data/finn.db`): 281 announcements,
extracted Q2 FY27 results, management-change bios, price history, and cached research for
**RELIANCE, BAJFINANCE, TCS and ITC**. A fresh deployment works immediately, with no pipeline run.

## Architecture

```
 NSE / BSE APIs ──▶ announcements.py ─┐
 Yahoo Finance  ──▶ prices.py ────────┤                      ┌────────────────────────────┐
 Screener.in    ──▶ fundamentals.py ──┤                      │  frontend/ (static SPA)    │
   (PDFs → PyMuPDF → 3k-char chunks)  ▼                      │  Tailwind + ES modules     │
                               ┌──────────────┐   JSON/HTTP  │  Today · Research · Chat   │
 pipeline/ classify, results,  │  SQLite      │◀────────────▶│  (served by FastAPI or any │
 mgmt_change, alerts, research │  finn.db     │  backend/    │   static host)             │
        │                      └──────────────┘  main.py     └────────────────────────────┘
        ▼                                         (FastAPI)
  llm.py: Gemini routing — call_cheap / call_strong, key + model fallback, cost log
```

| Layer | Technology |
|---|---|
| API | FastAPI + Uvicorn (also serves the frontend at `/`) |
| Storage | SQLite (one file, tracked in git for the demo data) |
| Documents | PyMuPDF text extraction, ~3,000-character overlapping chunks, dependency-free BM25 retrieval |
| LLM | Google Gemini via `google-genai`; cheap model for bulk extraction, stronger model (high thinking) for Promised vs. Delivered; automatic key and model fallback; every call logged with token counts and estimated cost |
| Frontend | Static single-page app: Tailwind (CDN) + vanilla ES modules, mobile-first (bottom tabs on phones, top tabs on desktop) |

### How answers stay grounded
Every source passage gets an id. The model may cite ids only; the readable citation ("AR FY26, p. 42")
is built in code from stored metadata, so a page number cannot be invented. Items without a valid citation
are dropped, and a quoted commitment is kept only if it really appears in the cited passage. Numbers from
results filings are checked against the PDF text before they are stored. Details and the reasoning behind each
choice are in [`DECISIONS.md`](DECISIONS.md).

## Local quickstart

Requires Python 3.11+ (developed on 3.13).

```bash
python -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\activate            # Windows   (macOS/Linux: source .venv/bin/activate)
pip install -r backend/requirements.txt

copy backend\.env.example backend\.env      # macOS/Linux: cp
# edit backend/.env and set GEMINI_API_KEY (free key: https://aistudio.google.com/apikey)

uvicorn backend.main:app --port 8000
```

Open <http://localhost:8000>. The Today and Research tabs work from the bundled database even without a key;
a key is only needed for Ask FINN, research on new tickers, and re-running the AI pipeline steps.
API docs are at <http://localhost:8000/docs>.

### Refreshing the data (optional)
Run from the repo root, in this order:

```bash
python -m backend.data.prices                    # Yahoo Finance prices
python -m backend.data.announcements             # NSE (BSE fallback) filings, last 30 days
python -m backend.pipeline.classify              # categories, scores, summaries (LLM)
python -m backend.pipeline.results_extract       # results numbers from PDFs (LLM)
python -m backend.pipeline.mgmt_change           # management changes + bios (LLM + web search)
python -m backend.data.fundamentals              # Screener annual reports + concalls (no LLM)
python -m backend.pipeline.research RELIANCE     # research for a ticker (LLM)
```

The bundled prices end on 13 Nov 2026. Price/volume alerts ignore data older than 5 days, so they will stop
firing on a deployment until you run the price step again.

## Deployment

The app is one Python service that also serves the frontend, so a single web service is enough.
Neither option below has been run by the author; the commands are the standard ones for each platform.

### Option A — one service on Render (recommended)
1. Push this repo to GitHub.
2. Render dashboard → **New → Web Service** → connect the repo.
3. Settings: **Runtime** Python 3 · **Build command** `pip install -r backend/requirements.txt` ·
   **Start command** `uvicorn backend.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT`
4. **Environment**: `GEMINI_API_KEY` = your key, `GEMINI_BACKEND` = `gemini`, `PYTHON_VERSION` = `3.13.3`.
5. Deploy and open the service URL. (Railway works the same way: same build and start commands, same variables.)

`render.yaml` in the repo describes this setup if you prefer a Blueprint.

### Option B — frontend on Vercel, API on Render
1. Deploy the API as in Option A.
2. Edit `frontend/config.js` and set `window.FINN_API_URL = "https://<your-render-service>.onrender.com";`
3. Vercel → **Add New Project** → import the repo → **Root Directory** `frontend`, Framework preset **Other**, no build command.
4. CORS already allows any origin, so no backend change is needed.

## Engineering trade-offs and known limitations

- **Free-tier AI quota.** Free Gemini keys have daily limits per model. `llm.py` moves to the next key and then the next model
  when a limit is hit, which keeps things running, but answers may then come from a lighter model, and during
  heavy use or provider overload calls can still fail (the UI shows the error and lets you retry). `gemini-2.5-pro` is
  not available on new free projects, so the "strong" model is `gemini-3.5-flash` with high thinking. Its cost estimate
  is approximate.
- **Keyword search, not vector search.** Retrieval is BM25 over chunks: fast, free and easy to explain, but it misses
  synonyms ("bad loans" vs "NPA"). In testing, a Reliance ARPU question missed a relevant Q2 FY27 passage. Embeddings would improve recall.
- **Page numbers are PDF page positions**, not the numbers printed on the page, so they can differ by a few pages.
- **ITC has no concall transcripts on Screener.in** (the link is greyed out for every call), so its Promised vs. Delivered
  compares the annual report with the latest results only, and mostly returns "Partially Disclosed". Its annual report's
  forward-looking targets are largely sustainability goals. NSE/BSE earnings-call filings could fill the gap.
- **Statuses are AI judgement.** "Beat / On Track / Missed" is the model's reading of the cited passages. For example,
  Reliance's Jio ARPU growth of 3.5% against a "5–6%" aim is labelled Missed although management said about 4–5% in Q1. Read the cited page.
- **Quarter labels for concalls are derived from the call month**, since Screener shows no quarter. Off-cycle calls can be mislabelled.
- **Scraping fragility.** NSE, BSE and Screener are scraped without official APIs and can change or block cloud IP addresses,
  so refreshing data from a hosted server may fail even though it works locally. This is why the database is bundled.
- **Single-user, no authentication.** Alert settings are global, and anyone with the URL can call the AI endpoints and use your API quota.
  Fine for a demo; add authentication and rate limiting before real use.
- **Ephemeral storage on free hosts.** Render's free disk resets on each deploy, so research generated live and changed settings are lost
  on redeploy (the bundled database is restored). New-ticker research takes 1–2 minutes and free instances sleep when idle.
- **Tailwind is loaded from its CDN**, which is not meant for production; compiled CSS needs Node (not available where this was built).
- **Not financial advice.** Output is AI-generated from public documents; check the cited source before acting.

## Repository layout

```
backend/
  main.py            FastAPI app (also serves frontend/)
  llm.py             Gemini routing, fallback, usage/cost log
  config/            companies.json (18 portfolio + 4 research-demo companies)
  data/              prices.py, announcements.py, fundamentals.py, finn.db (tracked)
  pipeline/          classify, results_extract, mgmt_change, alerts, research, pdf_utils
  cache/             downloaded PDFs and raw API responses (git-ignored)
frontend/            index.html, config.js, js/ (today, research, chat, app)
ai-build-logs/       Claude Code session transcripts for this build (keys redacted)
DECISIONS.md         every technical decision and its reasoning
DEPLOY_AND_SUBMIT.md handoff and submission guide
```

# FINN — AI investment assistant for Indian retail investors

FINN turns the daily flood of NSE/BSE corporate filings into a short, sourced digest, and lets you
ask questions that are answered only from company documents. It was built as a small working product
for the ENAM AI Engineer assessment, on free-tier infrastructure.

| Feature | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Push digest** | Classifies and scores every filing for an 18-company portfolio into *Must Read / Worth a Look / Routine*, with a one-line "why it matters". Results filings show extracted revenue / EBITDA / PBT / PAT with QoQ and YoY; management-change filings show who is joining or leaving, with a short background. |
| **Alerts** | Volume spikes, large price moves and material filings, with thresholds and watched categories the user can change live. |
| **Deep research** | For any NSE ticker: overview, financial health, growth catalysts and risks, built from the latest annual report and concall transcripts (via Screener.in), every bullet cited to a document and page. |
| **Promised vs. Delivered** | Finds specific, measurable commitments management made (annual report, older concalls) and checks them against later concalls and the latest quarterly results, with a status (*Beat / On Track / Delayed or Missed / Partially Disclosed*). |
| **Ask FINN** | Chat that retrieves from the stored documents, filings, results and prices and answers with inline citations such as `[Concall Q1 FY27, p. 22]`. |

The repository ships with a pre-populated database (`backend/data/finn.db`): 281 announcements,
extracted Q2 FY27 results, management-change bios, price history, and cached research for
**RELIANCE, BAJFINANCE, TCS and ITC**. A fresh deployment works immediately, with no pipeline run.

## Architecture

```
 NSE / BSE APIs ──▶ announcements.py ─┐
 Yahoo Finance  ──▶ prices.py ────────┤                      ┌────────────────────────────┐
 Screener.in    ──▶ fundamentals.py ──┤                      │  frontend/ (static SPA)    │
   (PDFs → PyMuPDF → 3k-char chunks)  ▼                      │  Tailwind + ES modules     │
                               ┌──────────────┐   JSON/HTTP  │  Today · Research · Chat   │
 pipeline/ classify, results,  │  SQLite      │◀────────────▶│  (served by FastAPI or any │
 mgmt_change, alerts, research │  finn.db     │  backend/    │   static host)             │
        │                      └──────────────┘  main.py     └────────────────────────────┘
        ▼                                         (FastAPI)
  llm.py: Gemini routing — call_cheap / call_strong, key + model fallback, cost log
```

| Layer | Technology |
|---|---|
| API | FastAPI + Uvicorn (also serves the frontend at `/`) |
| Storage | SQLite (one file, tracked in git for the demo data) |
| Documents | PyMuPDF text extraction, ~3,000-character overlapping chunks, dependency-free BM25 retrieval |
| LLM | Google Gemini via `google-genai`; cheap model for bulk extraction, stronger model (high thinking) for Promised vs. Delivered; automatic key and model fallback; every call logged with token counts and estimated cost |
| Frontend | Static single-page app: Tailwind (CDN) + vanilla ES modules, mobile-first (bottom tabs on phones, top tabs on desktop) |

### How answers stay grounded
Every source passage gets an id. The model may cite ids only; the readable citation ("AR FY26, p. 42")
is built in code from stored metadata, so a page number cannot be invented. Items without a valid citation
are dropped, and a quoted commitment is kept only if it really appears in the cited passage. Numbers from
results filings are checked against the PDF text before they are stored. Details and the reasoning behind each
choice are in [`DECISIONS.md`](DECISIONS.md).

## Local quickstart

Requires Python 3.11+ (developed on 3.13).

```bash
python -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\activate            # Windows   (macOS/Linux: source .venv/bin/activate)
pip install -r backend/requirements.txt

copy backend\.env.example backend\.env      # macOS/Linux: cp
# edit backend/.env and set GEMINI_API_KEY (free key: https://aistudio.google.com/apikey)

uvicorn backend.main:app --port 8000
```

Open <http://localhost:8000>. The Today and Research tabs work from the bundled database even without a key;
a key is only needed for Ask FINN, research on new tickers, and re-running the AI pipeline steps.
API docs are at <http://localhost:8000/docs>.

### Refreshing the data (optional)
Run from the repo root, in this order:

```bash
python -m backend.data.prices                    # Yahoo Finance prices
python -m backend.data.announcements             # NSE (BSE fallback) filings, last 30 days
python -m backend.pipeline.classify              # categories, scores, summaries (LLM)
python -m backend.pipeline.results_extract       # results numbers from PDFs (LLM)
python -m backend.pipeline.mgmt_change           # management changes + bios (LLM + web search)
python -m backend.data.fundamentals              # Screener annual reports + concalls (no LLM)
python -m backend.pipeline.research RELIANCE     # research for a ticker (LLM)
```

The bundled prices end on 13 Nov 2026. Price/volume alerts ignore data older than 5 days, so they will stop
firing on a deployment until you run the price step again.

## Deployment

The app is one Python service that also serves the frontend, so a single web service is enough.
Neither option below has been run by the author; the commands are the standard ones for each platform.

### Option A — one service on Render (recommended)
1. Push this repo to GitHub.
2. Render dashboard → **New → Web Service** → connect the repo.
3. Settings: **Runtime** Python 3 · **Build command** `pip install -r backend/requirements.txt` ·
   **Start command** `uvicorn backend.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT`
4. **Environment**: `GEMINI_API_KEY` = your key, `GEMINI_BACKEND` = `gemini`, `PYTHON_VERSION` = `3.13.3`.
5. Deploy and open the service URL. (Railway works the same way: same build and start commands, same variables.)

`render.yaml` in the repo describes this setup if you prefer a Blueprint.

### Option B — frontend on Vercel, API on Render
1. Deploy the API as in Option A.
2. Edit `frontend/config.js` and set `window.FINN_API_URL = "https://<your-render-service>.onrender.com";`
3. Vercel → **Add New Project** → import the repo → **Root Directory** `frontend`, Framework preset **Other**, no build command.
4. CORS already allows any origin, so no backend change is needed.

## Engineering trade-offs and known limitations

- **Free-tier AI quota.** Free Gemini keys have daily limits per model. `llm.py` moves to the next key and then the next model
  when a limit is hit, which keeps things running, but answers may then come from a lighter model, and during
  heavy use or provider overload calls can still fail (the UI shows the error and lets you retry). `gemini-2.5-pro` is
  not available on new free projects, so the "strong" model is `gemini-3.5-flash` with high thinking. Its cost estimate
  is approximate.
- **Keyword search, not vector search.** Retrieval is BM25 over chunks: fast, free and easy to explain, but it misses
  synonyms ("bad loans" vs "NPA"). In testing, a Reliance ARPU question missed a relevant Q2 FY27 passage. Embeddings would improve recall.
- **Page numbers are PDF page positions**, not the numbers printed on the page, so they can differ by a few pages.
- **ITC has no concall transcripts on Screener.in** (the link is greyed out for every call), so its Promised vs. Delivered
  compares the annual report with the latest results only, and mostly returns "Partially Disclosed". Its annual report's
  forward-looking targets are largely sustainability goals. NSE/BSE earnings-call filings could fill the gap.
- **Statuses are AI judgement.** "Beat / On Track / Missed" is the model's reading of the cited passages. For example,
  Reliance's Jio ARPU growth of 3.5% against a "5–6%" aim is labelled Missed although management said about 4–5% in Q1. Read the cited page.
- **Quarter labels for concalls are derived from the call month**, since Screener shows no quarter. Off-cycle calls can be mislabelled.
- **Scraping fragility.** NSE, BSE and Screener are scraped without official APIs and can change or block cloud IP addresses,
  so refreshing data from a hosted server may fail even though it works locally. This is why the database is bundled.
- **Single-user, no authentication.** Alert settings are global, and anyone with the URL can call the AI endpoints and use your API quota.
  Fine for a demo; add authentication and rate limiting before real use.
- **Ephemeral storage on free hosts.** Render's free disk resets on each deploy, so research generated live and changed settings are lost
  on redeploy (the bundled database is restored). New-ticker research takes 1–2 minutes and free instances sleep when idle.
- **Tailwind is loaded from its CDN**, which is not meant for production; compiled CSS needs Node (not available where this was built).
- **Not financial advice.** Output is AI-generated from public documents; check the cited source before acting.

## Repository layout

```
backend/
  main.py            FastAPI app (also serves frontend/)
  llm.py             Gemini routing, fallback, usage/cost log
  config/            companies.json (18 portfolio + 4 research-demo companies)
  data/              prices.py, announcements.py, fundamentals.py, finn.db (tracked)
  pipeline/          classify, results_extract, mgmt_change, alerts, research, pdf_utils
  cache/             downloaded PDFs and raw API responses (git-ignored)
frontend/            index.html, config.js, js/ (today, research, chat, app)
ai-build-logs/       Claude Code session transcripts for this build (keys redacted)
DECISIONS.md         every technical decision and its reasoning
DEPLOY_AND_SUBMIT.md handoff and submission guide
```

# FINN — Financial Investment Assistant

FINN is a mobile-first financial investment assistant, built as a small, working
product for the ENAM AI Engineer assessment.

> **Status:** Project skeleton only. No features are implemented yet.

## Tech Stack

| Layer           | Technology                              |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| Backend API     | Python, FastAPI                         |
| Database        | SQLite                                  |
| Data processing | Python                                  |
| Frontend        | Next.js (responsive, mobile-first)      |

Backend and frontend are separate projects that talk over HTTP (JSON).

## Folder Structure

```
FINN/
├── backend/         Everything Python
│   ├── config/      Configuration (companies.json: portfolio + research_demo lists)
│   ├── data/        prices.py, announcements.py (ingestion) and finn.db (git-ignored)
│   ├── pipeline/    Processing: classify.py (announcement categories, scores, summaries)
│   ├── llm.py       Gemini model routing (call_cheap / call_strong) + token/cost logging
│   └── cache/       Raw API responses + BSE code map, for offline replay (git-ignored)
├── app/             Next.js frontend (mobile-first UI)
├── README.md
├── DECISIONS.md Log of technical decisions and their reasoning
└── .gitignore
```

### Purpose of each folder

- **`backend/`** — The FastAPI application. Exposes a JSON API to the frontend,
  reads from the SQLite database, and contains the assistant's logic. It does
  not fetch raw data itself; that is the pipeline's job.
- **`backend/config/`** — All configurable values live here rather than in code.
  `companies.json` defines two lists: `portfolio` (18 NSE companies for the mock
  portfolio) and `research_demo` (4 companies, 2 of them outside the portfolio).
  Tickers are never hard-coded elsewhere. Secrets (API keys) go in environment
  variables / `.env`, not here.
- **`backend/data/`** — Holds raw input files and the SQLite database. Contents are
  git-ignored so the repo stays small; the pipeline can regenerate them.
- **`backend/pipeline/`** — Standalone Python scripts that ingest data, process it, and
  write results into SQLite. Runs independently of the API (manually or on a
  schedule).
- **`backend/cache/`** — Short-lived cache (e.g. external API responses) to avoid
  repeated network calls. Everything here is disposable and git-ignored.
- **`app/`** — The Next.js frontend. Designed for phone screens first, scaling
  up to tablet and desktop. Calls the backend API only.

## Architecture Overview

```
  ┌──────────────┐     reads       ┌──────────────┐
  │   config/    │ ──────────────▶ │  pipeline/   │  Python: fetch → clean → store
  └──────────────┘                 └──────┬───────┘
                                          │ writes (uses cache/ for raw responses)
                                          ▼
                                   ┌──────────────┐
                                   │ data/ SQLite │
                                   └──────┬───────┘
                                          │ reads
                                          ▼
                                   ┌──────────────┐
                                   │  backend/    │  FastAPI JSON API
                                   └──────┬───────┘
                                          │ HTTP / JSON
                                          ▼
                                   ┌──────────────┐
                                   │    app/      │  Next.js, mobile-first
                                   └──────────────┘
```

**Flow:**

1. `pipeline/` reads the list of companies from `config/`, gathers and
   processes data, and stores it in SQLite under `data/`.
2. `backend/` serves that data (plus any assistant logic) through a FastAPI
   JSON API.
3. `app/` is the user-facing Next.js interface that calls the API.

This keeps each part simple, independently runnable, and easy to deploy:
SQLite needs no database server, the backend is a single Python process, and
